source.title: Path-SGD: Path-Normalized Optimization in Deep Neural Networks
source.authors: Behnam Neyshabur; R. Salakhutdinov; N. Srebro

record.tranche_reason: Compares an adaptive optimizer (AdaGrad) with SGD and reports training and test error, using benchmark experiments rather than the optimizer comparisons in V4.
record.gate_note: The paper also compares Path-SGD with SGD and AdaGrad, and reports balanced versus rescaled unbalanced initializations and dropout conditions. Those results do not test the other claim versions. No random-label, width, architecture, large-batch, dropout-effect, sharpness, or memorized-example-removal experiment is reported.
record.test_reason: The study compares AdaGrad with SGD on four image-classification datasets after validation-based step-size selection, bearing on V4. Its matched experiments with and without dropout also bear on V6. The supplied text contains plot axes and legends but no recoverable curve values or explicit outcomes for either comparison.
record.authors_conclusion: The record is broadly accurate. The authors conclude that Path-SGD can reach comparable accuracy faster and sometimes attain better generalization, including when training error is zero. They present this as proof-of-concept evidence and suggest implicit regularization as an explanation; the advantage is not universal.
record.recipe_differences: Compares Path-SGD, SGD and AdaGrad on image classification benchmarks; the V4 comparison is limited to AdaGrad versus SGD, not Adam or language benchmarks.
record.method_sensitivity: Initialization balance affects SGD and AdaGrad: the authors say unbalanced initialization considerably hurts their performance. Dropout condition changes the reported optimizer comparisons, though no AdaGrad-versus-SGD test-error outcome is stated in the text for either condition.

fits_no_version.finding: Path-SGD sometimes achieves lower final test error than SGD and AdaGrad and often reaches comparable performance faster. SGD slightly outperforms Path-SGD on CIFAR-100 without dropout.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Path-normalized optimization can improve convergence and held-out performance relative to SGD and AdaGrad in the tested fully connected ReLU networks.

fits_no_version.finding: Rescaling-equivalent unbalanced initializations substantially impair SGD and AdaGrad, while Path-SGD produces identical learning curves under balanced and unbalanced initialization.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Optimization performance can depend on function-preserving weight rescaling; Path-SGD is invariant to this rescaling.

record.problems: The relevant AdaGrad-versus-SGD test-error results are shown only in plots, with no numerical values or dataset-specific textual comparison. The experiments use feed-forward networks with two 4000-unit hidden layers and four image datasets.
record.rows_left_out: No rows left out. Other reported comparisons concern Path-SGD versus SGD or Path-SGD versus AdaGrad, rather than the adaptive-optimizer-versus-SGD comparison named in V4.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and comparison with natural-label held-out accuracy.
Width dependence beyond the width needed to fit the training data.
Convolutional versus fully connected architectures and local connectivity.
Adam, language benchmarks, momentum-SGD comparisons, broader hyperparameter tuning, decoupled weight decay, and switching optimizers.
Batch-size comparisons and recipes for removing large-batch penalties.
Very small training sets, varying dropout strength to establish underfitting, convolutional classifiers, and removing dropout and weight decay together with data augmentation.
Magnitude-aware sharpness, its correlation with generalization gaps, and comparisons with other measures.

missing.what: AdaGrad-versus-SGD training and test comparisons with dropout for all four datasets. Recover the curves before assigning outcome states or verdicts.
AdaGrad-versus-SGD comparisons under unbalanced initialization and their dependence on training duration. The text says both methods deteriorate but does not establish their relative ordering.

Within-optimizer test-error comparisons between dropout and no dropout on all four datasets, using matched initialization and epoch counts. Dropout retains each unit with probability 0.5. These experiments test V6, contrary to the record's gate note, but their outcomes are unreadable in the supplied text.
missing.locator: Section 5; Figures 2 versus 3 and Figures 4 versus 5

record.verdict_notes: This study is not a listed original source. No directional verdict is justified from the supplied text: axis labels do not reveal curve ordering, and comparisons against Path-SGD do not establish AdaGrad-versus-SGD outcomes or dropout effects.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and natural-label generalization coexistence.

The paper compares AdaGrad with SGD on image datasets, but the supplied text gives no dataset-specific numerical or explicit textual result for that comparison; plotted values are not recoverable from the text. Adam, language benchmarks, broader tuning, decoupled weight decay, and switching from Adam to SGD are not tested.
Whether dropout lowers test error or underfits.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its relation to the generalization gap.
Removing memorized training examples and measuring test accuracy.
